gloss: grief · sorrow — and, in Buddhist texts, compassion (karuṇā)
formNote: The Shuowen: 悲，痛也。从心，非聲 — “pain; from heart, with 非 as the sound.” Reading the graph as “not-heart” is folk etymology: 非 contributes the sound, not the sense.
summary: Grief, sorrow, being pained. Buddhist translators used it for karuṇā, compassion, the wish that beings be free from suffering: a word for sorrow, chosen for the wish to end it.
placement: On the right of the sphere's equator, mirroring 慈: the two halves of 慈悲. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: Compassion, and Great Compassion
satellites.evidence: 悲 renders karuṇā, the second of the Four Immeasurables. The Abhidharmakośa distinguishes that immeasurable from a Buddha’s great compassion (大悲, mahākaruṇā), which it counts among the qualities unique to a Buddha.

cites.locator: ch. 7 分別智品: 大悲

gaps: The Kośa locator for 大悲 is Baracus’s recollection; open T1558 ch. 7 and record the passage.

satellites.title: The Grief of Autumn
satellites.evidence: 九辯 in the Chuci opens 悲哉，秋之為氣也 — “how grievous is the air of autumn!” — and made autumn sorrow (悲秋) a lasting theme of Chinese poetry. This is 悲’s native register, a personal grief, before the Buddhist sense.
satellites.caveat: 九辯 is traditionally attributed to Song Yu (宋玉); the attribution is traditional.
